name: The Expensive Mistake Countdown
why_it_works: Fear of loss pulls harder than the hope of gain. Counting down from 3 to 1 promises that the worst mistake is still coming, so people stay for number one. Putting a price on that mistake makes the fix feel urgent, and the expert who names the price becomes the obvious person to call.

hook.pattern: Promise three mistakes around a task the viewer is about to do, and tell them the last one costs the most.

variables.name: audience_task
variables.description: What the viewer is doing, as a short -ing phrase

variables.name: mistake_3
variables.example: Listing photos taken on a cloudy afternoon

variables.name: mistake_2
variables.example: Pricing to match the neighbor's asking price, not the sold price

variables.name: mistake_1
variables.description: The costly mistake, the reason to watch

variables.name: cost_of_mistake_1
variables.description: What mistake 1 typically costs, honest and specific

variables.name: fix_1
variables.example: Inspect before you list so repairs are on your schedule, not the buyer's

variables.name: offer
variables.example: DM 'LIST' for our free pre-listing checklist

beats.purpose: hook: promise the countdown and the price
beats.voiceover: Three mistakes people make {{audience_task}}. Number one is the expensive one.

visual.prompt: Vertical 9:16 photo of a large bold numeral 3 printed on a card held up in front of a scene tied to {{audience_task}}, soft daylight, shallow depth of field
Vertical photo showing the mistake '{{mistake_3}}' in an everyday setting, slightly flat unflattering light, mid shot
Vertical photo illustrating '{{mistake_2}}', a person looking at paperwork or a screen with mild concern, desk lamp light, over-the-shoulder framing

beats.purpose: mistake 1: the costly one, with motion
beats.voiceover: And number one: {{mistake_1}}. That can cost {{cost_of_mistake_1}}.

visual.prompt: Vertical 9:16 slow push-in on a scene showing the consequence of '{{mistake_1}}', a frustrated person reading a bill or report, moody late-day light
Vertical photo of a {{brand}} professional calmly walking a client through the fix '{{fix_1}}', bright tidy office or on-site, warm light, eye-level two-shot

slides.headline: 3 mistakes {{audience_task}}
slides.body: Number 1 costs the most. Swipe to the end.
slides.visual_prompt: Bold title slide in {{brand}} colors with a large numeral 3 and a subtle background photo tied to {{audience_task}}

slides.headline: Mistake 3
slides.visual_prompt: Photo showing '{{mistake_3}}' in an everyday setting, flat light, large numeral 3 in the corner

slides.headline: Mistake 2
slides.visual_prompt: Photo of a person frowning at paperwork illustrating '{{mistake_2}}', large numeral 2 in the corner

slides.headline: Mistake 1: the expensive one
slides.visual_prompt: Moody photo showing the consequence of '{{mistake_1}}', large red numeral 1 in the corner

slides.headline: The fix
slides.visual_prompt: Bright photo of a {{brand}} professional helping a client, warm light, check mark graphic

slides.headline: Want help with this?
slides.visual_prompt: Clean {{brand}} logo card with the offer in large type and a save icon

craft.technique: Reverse countdown with a priced payoff
craft.notes: Order the mistakes from cheapest to most expensive so tension rises, and put a concrete cost on number 1 only. One price is believable; three prices feel like a sales pitch. Keep mistakes 3 and 2 under four seconds each.

do_not: Inflate the cost of mistake 1; use a range you would defend to a client
Make mistake 1 something only your paid service can fix; give a fix they could act on
Use generic mistakes like 'not doing research'; each one should be a specific action
compliance: Real estate: follow fair housing rules; never describe buyers, sellers or neighborhoods by protected class; include brokerage name and license where your state requires
Real estate and mortgage: no guarantees of sale price, timeline or savings; say 'can cost', not 'will cost'
Mortgage: show the NMLS number; any rate or payment figure needs APR and terms, or leave numbers out
